vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: aicreditshare-platform
Version: 1.0.7

The skill bundle is a legitimate integration for the AI Credit Share platform, providing a CLI tool and agent instructions for task and skill management. The scripts (init.sh and aics.sh) use standard security practices such as HMAC-SHA256 for API authentication and 'jq' for safe JSON construction to prevent injection. It stores its own platform-specific credentials in ~/.aicreditshare/config.json and communicates exclusively with the stated domain (aicreditshare.com) without any evidence of data exfiltration, malicious execution, or harmful prompt injection.

llm.summary: The skill's code and instructions match its stated purpose (automating an AI Credit Share account and actions) but it has some minor coherence and security hygiene issues you should review before use.

dimensions.detail: The name/description describe automating an AI Credit Share platform and the scripts and SKILL.md implement calls to https://www.aicreditshare.com APIs for registration, tasks, skills, balance, etc. This is coherent. Minor mismatch: the manifest declares no required binaries/env-vars but the shipped scripts in fact need curl, jq and openssl.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and the scripts stay within the platform domain (they call only https://www.aicreditshare.com endpoints). The runtime instructions and scripts read and write a local config (~/.aicreditshare/config.json) and the SKILL.md documents saving API keys/secrets. No instructions attempt to read unrelated system files or exfiltrate data to unrelated endpoints. Note: SKILL.md documents an event polling behavior; the scripts don't create a background daemon themselves (polling would need to be run by the agent/user).
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec (instruction-only) which lowers risk. However the package includes shell scripts that will create ~/.aicreditshare/config.json when run. The scripts extract and persist credentials to disk (the archive is written only when user runs the provided scripts).
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request cloud credentials or unrelated secrets. It optionally uses an environment variable AICREDITSHARE_DEFAULT_PASSWORD (documented) and otherwise stores/uses the platform API key/secret returned by the service. These credentials are appropriate for the skill's purpose, but they are persisted to a local file by the scripts—this storage should be reviewed.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always:true and does not modify other skills. It writes its own config file under the user's home directory (~/.aicreditshare/config.json) when registering/logging in. The script does not set restrictive file permissions, so the saved API secret may be world-readable depending on system umask—this is a security hygiene concern rather than a capability mismatch.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This skill appears to do what it says (automates actions against aicreditshare.com) but review and take these precautions before installing or running it:

- Verify the platform URL and origin: confirm https://www.aicreditshare.com is the legitimate service you intend to use. The skill talks only to that hostname.
- Inspect the scripts yourself before running: scripts/init.sh will POST registration/login data and write credentials to ~/.aicreditshare/config.json; scripts/aics.sh will read that file and make signed API calls.
- Install required tools: curl, jq and openssl are used by the scripts but are not declared in the package metadata. Ensure they are present and up-to-date on your system.
- Protect saved credentials: the scripts create ~/.aicreditshare/config.json but do not explicitly set restrictive permissions. After registration/login, run chmod 600 ~/.aicreditshare/config.json so only your user can read it.
- Consider using a unique account/password: if you are uncomfortable storing secrets, create an account dedicated to this automation rather than using high-value credentials.
- If you want autonomous polling, understand that polling must be run by you or the agent; the package does not install a background service. Only grant autonomous invocation if you trust the skill and its access to your agent.

If any of the above concerns (unexpected endpoints, additional hidden network calls, or requests for unrelated credentials) appear, do not run the scripts and ask the publisher for clarification.
